messages.subject: Arranging input elements in one row
parts:
Hi all,

I've created this panel below, but I want to have everything (both the text and the input elements) arranged together in one row. My instinct is that I'll need to do something in CSS to get this to work, but I'm not very sure how exactly. I think I tried wrapping everything together with div(class = "row-fluid", ...), but that didn't work. What would be the easiest way to do so? Thanks!

Current interface:

Desired interface:

Q: What is probability that (total CP) in the year (2015) is (above) (50)%? A: 0%


Code:
output$targetPanelExisting1 <- renderUI ({
  wellPanel(
    p("Q: What is the probability that "),
    selectInput("indicatorpview", "",
                choices = c("total CP" = "Total", 
                            "modern CP" = "Modern", 
                            "traditional CP" = "Traditional", 
                            "unmet need in FP" = "Unmet",
                            "total demand in FP" = "TotalPlusUnmet", 
                            "demand in FP (excl modern)" = "TradPlusUnmet" 
                ), selected = "total CP"),
    br(" in the year "),
    numericInput("yearpview", "", 2015, 
                 min = 1990, max = 2015, step = 1),
    br(" is "),
    selectInput("booleanpview", "",
                choices = c("above" = ">", 
                            # "at least" = ">=", 
                            "below" = "<"
                            #, "at most" = "<="
                ), selected = "above"),
    numericInput("percInputview", "", 50,
                 min = 0, max = 100, step = 1),
    br("%?"),
    br("A:"),
    strong(textOutput("postprobOutputExisting"))
  )
})

- JinRou

messages.subject: Re: Arranging input elements in one row
parts:
Hi Jin Rou,

The only way I can think of to ease the pain a little is by defining a wrap.with.span function. 

But of course by default the spans should sum up to 12 so the below is not right! But it serves to illustrate the idea.

Actually I usually stick to HTML ui and that is easier to set the width of the dropdowns. Currently it's quite awkward. Maybe I will try to address this with an update to ShinySky soon.


library(shiny)

wrap.with.span <- function( ...,size = rep(1,length(list(...)))) {
args <- list(...)
i <- 0
result <- lapply(args,function(a) {
i <<- i + 1
div(args[[i]],class=paste0("span",size[i]))
})
return(result)
}

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$targetPanelExisting1 <- renderUI ({
  wellPanel(
wrap.with.span(

p("Q: What is the probability that "),
  selectInput("indicatorpview", "",
  choices = c("total CP" = "Total", 
  "modern CP" = "Modern", 
  "traditional CP" = "Traditional", 
  "unmet need in FP" = "Unmet",
  "total demand in FP" = "TotalPlusUnmet", 
  "demand in FP (excl modern)" = "TradPlusUnmet" 
  ), selected = "total CP"),
HTML(" in the year "),

numericInput("yearpview", "", 2015, 
  min = 1990, max = 2015, step = 1),
HTML(" is "),

selectInput("booleanpview", "",
  choices = c("above" = ">", 
  # "at least" = ">=", 
  "below" = "<"
  #, "at most" = "<="
  ), selected = "above"),
  numericInput("percInputview", "", 50,
  min = 0, max = 100, step = 1),

HTML("%?"),
  HTML("A:"),
  strong(textOutput("postprobOutputExisting"))
                , size = c(2,3,1,2,0,3,3,1,1))
  )
  })
})
